$comment: Per-repo config for THIS repo's own ratcheted PR/push source-leak run (self-source-leak-gate.yml passes it via the reusable gate's `config` input; consuming repos never receive it). ONE exemption class, the same self-referential false positive config/self-check.json documents at length: files that must carry a gate's OWN literal name, which the SLG_PLANNING_DOC rule reads as a planning-artifact marker. skills-drift-gate.yml is the gate's own reusable workflow — its steps invoke scripts out of the gate checkout directory named after the gate, an irreducible reference (all rephraseable prose mentions on changed lines are reworded instead, per the rephrase-first doctrine). self-check.json is the hermetic self-check's exemption ledger — its entries LIST such gate filenames verbatim, so any edit to the ledger line would otherwise trip the ratchet that this config exists to calibrate. This file itself is self-exempt (the engine exempts the --config path). The parity fixture corpus is skipped by prefix and lines marked source-leak-allow are exempt: planted detector test input and the engine's own rationale comments must be able to carry the phrasings the gate bans. Engine+test pair exemption: source-leak-gate.test.mjs and source-leak-ratchet.test.mjs carry the private names AS deliberate test inputs, scattered through the whole file (the same class as the other engine+test pairs the org exempts). The ENGINE and its FIXTURE are deliberately NOT exempted here. Neither needs a whole-file exemption and both are actively harmed by one: the engine already protects exactly the region that must carry the markers — the sentinel-bracketed rule definitions — and scans the rest of itself normally, so a whole-file exemption would discard a real leak anywhere outside that region; the fixture is path-exempt by the engine itself (it is skipped by real path, never scanned on a repo walk), so listing it here bought nothing. A marker-bearing line that the engine must carry OUTSIDE the rule-definition region is exempted at the LINE with source-leak-allow, never by re-adding the file.
